mainTopic: Witnesses and students arguing in capital cases, רב's rule that a judge may switch from זכות to חובה at the verdict, and the rule that one reason from two פסוקים counts as one vote
overview: The גמרא first explains why רבי יוסי בר יהודה lets a witness argue for acquittal: the פסוק bans a witness only from speaking 'למות'. The רבנן say a witness looks biased, so he may not argue at all, and they use 'למות' to teach that a student may not argue for guilt. Next, רב limits the משנה's rule against switching from זכות to חובה to the discussion stage, and says switching is allowed at the גמר דין. The גמרא challenges רב four times: from the next-morning session, from the deadlocked judges, from a student who died, and from the scribes who write down the זכות reasons. Each challenge is answered. The last answer is that the scribes write the reasons so that two judges who give one reason from two פסוקים count as one vote. That rule comes from רבי יוחנן, and its source is the פסוקים 'אחת דבר אלהים' and 'כפטיש יפוצץ סלע'. רב זביד offers an example of one reason from two sources from a משנה about the מזבח, but it is rejected because רבי יהושע and רבן גמליאל really disagree. רב פפא begins a new example from a ברייתא of רבי יוסי הגלילי, which continues on the next amud.

steps.title: What is the source for רבי יוסי בר יהודה?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks for the reason behind רבי יוסי בר יהודה's view that a witness may argue for acquittal.
steps.simpleTranslation: What is the reason of רבי יוסי בר יהודה?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks what source supports רבי יוסי בר יהודה's view that a witness may argue in the accused's favor. This question sets up the answer in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Earlier, רבי יוסי בר יהודה allowed a witness to speak up for acquittal, while the רבנן did not. The גמרא now wants to know what his view is based on.

phrases.aramaic: מַאי טַעְמָא דְּרַבִּי יוֹסֵי בַּר יְהוּדָה?
phrases.english: What is the reason of Rabbi Yosei bar Yehuda?

steps.triggerLanguage: מַאי טַעְמָא דְּרַבִּי יוֹסֵי בַּר יְהוּדָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Opens by asking for the source of a view stated just before this section.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The scriptural source for allowing a witness to argue for acquittal.

steps.title: The verse says 'that he die', so a witness may speak for acquittal
steps.stepSummary: The פסוק blocks a witness only from arguing for death, so he may argue for acquittal.
steps.simpleTranslation: Because the פסוק says, 'One witness shall not testify against a person that he die.' He may not speak up so that the accused will die, but he may speak up so that the accused will be acquitted.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that רבי יוסי בר יהודה reads the word 'למות' as a limit. A witness may not argue for death, but he may argue for life.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The extra word 'למות' narrows the ban to arguments that lead to execution. Arguments that help the accused are not included in the ban, so they are allowed.

keyTerms.meaning: Shall not testify or speak up
That he die, meaning toward a death sentence

phrases.english: As the verse states:
"One witness shall not testify against a person that he die."
It is for death that he does not speak,
but for acquittal he does speak.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 1.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The word 'למות' limits the ban to arguments for death, so arguing for acquittal is allowed.

steps.title: The רבנן's reason: a witness looks biased
steps.stepSummary: ריש לקיש explains that the רבנן forbid a witness to argue at all, because he looks like he has a personal stake.
steps.simpleTranslation: And what about the רבנן? ריש לקיש said: It is because the witness looks like someone who has a personal interest in his testimony.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks why the רבנן disagree, and ריש לקיש answers: a witness who argues, even for acquittal, looks biased.
steps.deeperAnalysis: For the רבנן, the problem is not what the פסוק allows. The problem is how it looks when a witness argues. Someone who already testified is not neutral, so his arguments are not heard.

keyTerms.meaning: Someone with a personal stake in his own testimony

phrases.english: And the Rabbis?
phrases.notes: He means: why don't the רבנן let a witness argue for acquittal?

phrases.english: Reish Lakish said:
Because he appears as one with a personal stake in his testimony.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Turns from רבי יוסי בר יהודה's reason to the reason of the רבנן.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: A witness who argues looks biased, so the court does not listen to him.

steps.title: What do the רבנן learn from 'that he die'?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks how the רבנן use the word 'למות' if they don't read it the way רבי יוסי בר יהודה does.
steps.simpleTranslation: And the רבנן, what do they learn from this word 'that he die'?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks what the word 'למות' teaches according to the רבנן. This sets up their answer in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The word 'למות' must teach something. Since the רבנן don't use it to allow a witness to argue for acquittal, the גמרא asks what they learn from it instead.

keyTerms.meaning: They expound or learn from it

phrases.english: And the Rabbis, this word "that he die",
what do they expound from it?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Follows up on the רבנן's view by asking how they use the word רבי יוסי בר יהודה relied on.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: What the word 'למות' teaches according to the רבנן.

steps.title: The רבנן apply 'that he die' to a student
steps.stepSummary: The רבנן use 'למות' to teach a rule about one of the students who sit in court.
steps.simpleTranslation: They apply it to one of the students.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that the רבנן read 'למות' as a rule about a student, not about a witness.
steps.deeperAnalysis: So the word 'למות' is not wasted according to the רבנן. It teaches that a student may not argue for death, while the witness rule comes from the first part of the פסוק.

keyTerms.meaning: They apply it, they set it in a case
The students who sat before the court in capital cases

phrases.english: They establish it as referring to one of the students.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers step 4.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: 'למות' teaches that a student's argument for guilt is not heard.

steps.title: A ברייתא: no witness arguing for acquittal, no student arguing for guilt
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא learns two rules from the פסוק: a witness's argument for acquittal is not heard, and a student's argument for guilt is not heard.
steps.simpleTranslation: As a ברייתא teaches: If one of the witnesses said, 'I have a reason to acquit him,' how do we know the court does not listen to him? The פסוק says, 'One witness shall not testify.' And if one of the students said, 'I have a reason to find him guilty,' how do we know the court does not listen to him? The פסוק says, 'One shall not testify against a person that he die.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a ברייתא that splits the פסוק into two lessons. The first part is about a witness, and 'למות' is about a student.
steps.deeperAnalysis: 'עד אחד לא יענה' blocks a witness from arguing at all, even for acquittal, just as the רבנן hold. 'אחד לא יענה בנפש למות' is read about any one person, meaning a student, and 'למות' limits that ban to arguing for death. So a student may argue for acquittal but not for guilt.

keyTerms.meaning: To present an argument for acquittal
To present an argument for guilt
The court does not listen to him

steps.whatToRemember: According to the רבנן: a witness may not argue at all, and a student may argue for acquittal but not for guilt. רבי יוסי בר יהודה lets a witness argue for acquittal.
steps.confusionAlert: The same פסוק is quoted twice for two different people. The first quote is about a witness, and the second, ending with 'למות', is about a student.

phrases.english: As it is taught in a baraita:
If one of the witnesses said:
"I have a reason to teach in his favor,"
from where do we know that they do not listen to him?
The verse states: "One witness shall not testify."
From where do we know regarding one of the students
who said, "I have a reason to teach against him,"
from where do we know that they do not listen to him?

phrases.aramaic: תַּלְמוּד לוֹמַר: ״אֶחָד לֹא יַעֲנֶה בְנֶפֶשׁ לָמוּת״.
phrases.english: The verse states: "One shall not testify against a person that he die."
phrases.notes: Here 'one' means any single person, like a student, and 'that he die' limits the ban to arguing for guilt.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Supports step 5 with a ברייתא.
steps.raayaObject: That the רבנן use 'למות' for a student's argument for guilt.
steps.raayaSupportSource: A ברייתא that learns the witness rule from 'עד אחד לא יענה' and the student rule from 'למות'.

steps.title: רב: the no-switching rule applies only during deliberation
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the משנה's rule about switching sides, and רב limits it to the discussion stage. At the verdict stage, someone who argued for acquittal may switch to guilt.
steps.simpleTranslation: The משנה said: In דיני נפשות, someone who argues for guilt may switch to acquittal, but not the other way around. רב said: This was taught only during the discussion. But when the verdict is being given, someone who argued for acquittal may switch and argue for guilt.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא moves to a new line in the משנה, the rule about switching sides. רב says this rule applies only while the judges are still discussing the case.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה protects the accused: once a judge argues for acquittal, he cannot argue for guilt. רב limits this to the discussion stage. At the final vote, a judge may change his mind toward guilt.

keyTerms.meaning: They taught this only in the case of

steps.whyThisMatters: רב makes the protection for the accused depend on the stage of the trial. The next step challenges exactly this distinction.

phrases.english: Capital cases: one who teaches, etc.
phrases.notes: כו׳ means 'and so on.' The rest of the משנה says one who argued for acquittal can't switch to guilt.

phrases.english: Rav said:

phrases.aramaic: לֹא שָׁנוּ אֶלָּא בִּשְׁעַת מַשָּׂא וּמַתָּן,
phrases.english: They taught this only at the time of deliberation,
but at the time of the verdict,
one who taught for acquittal may switch and teach for guilt.

steps.triggerLanguage: דִּינֵי נְפָשׁוֹת: הַמְלַמֵּד כּוּ׳. אָמַר רַב: לֹא שָׁנוּ אֶלָּא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new topic from the next line of the משנה.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The ban on switching from acquittal to guilt applies only during deliberation, not at the verdict.

steps.title: Challenge from the next-morning session
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges רב from a משנה about the judges returning the next morning. Even then, at the verdict stage, someone who argued for acquittal cannot switch.
steps.simpleTranslation: The גמרא raises a challenge: The next day the judges get up early and come to court. The one who argued for acquittal says, 'I said acquit, and I still say acquit.' The one who argued for guilt says, 'I said guilty, and I still say guilty.' Someone who argued for guilt may switch to acquittal, but someone who argued for acquittal cannot switch to guilt.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא quotes a משנה that seems to go against רב. Step 9 spells out the problem, and step 10 answers it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The next-morning session is when the final verdict is given. Still, this משנה says someone who argued for acquittal cannot switch to guilt, which is exactly what רב allowed at the verdict stage.

keyTerms.meaning: The one who voted to acquit
The one who voted to convict
In my place, meaning I stand by my position

phrases.english: They raised an objection:
The next day they rise early and come.
The one who acquits says:
"I am the one who acquitted, and I acquit in my place."
The one who convicts says:
"I am the one who convicted, and I convict in my place."
One who taught for guilt may teach for acquittal,
but one who taught for acquittal
cannot switch and teach for guilt.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks רב's statement in step 7.
steps.kashyaTarget: רב's claim that at the verdict stage someone who argued for acquittal may switch to guilt.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The next-morning session is the verdict stage, yet the משנה still forbids switching from acquittal to guilt.

steps.title: The next day counts as the verdict stage
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא spells out why the משנה from step 8 is a problem for רב: the next morning is the time of the גמר דין.
steps.simpleTranslation: But the next day is the time of the verdict!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא finishes the challenge from step 8. It explains why the next-morning case is a problem for רב.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב said switching from זכות to חובה is allowed at the גמר דין stage. The גמרא assumes that 'the next day' means the גמר דין stage. Yet the משנה says someone who argued for זכות still cannot switch then, so this seems to contradict רב.

phrases.english: But the next day
is the time of the verdict!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes the challenge begun in step 8
steps.kashyaTarget: רב's rule that switching from זכות to חובה is allowed at the גמר דין stage
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The משנה forbids switching on the next day, and the next day is the גמר דין stage.

steps.title: The next day also includes discussion
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers that the next day can also include משא ומתן. The משנה's ban on switching refers to that discussion time.
steps.simpleTranslation: And according to your reasoning, is there no discussion on the next day? When the משנה teaches this, it is talking about the time of discussion.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא defends רב. The next morning is not only for the verdict; the judges can keep discussing then too.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The challenge assumed that 'the next day' always means the גמר דין stage. The answer points out that משא ומתן can continue the next day as well. So the משנה's ban on switching applies during that discussion, which matches רב.

keyTerms.meaning: And according to your reasoning: your own logic works against you
Discussion and debate among the judges

phrases.english: And according to your reasoning,
is there no discussion on the next day?
When it teaches this, it is at the time of discussion.
phrases.notes: The 'it' is the משנה about the next morning: its ban on switching is about the discussion part of that day.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְלִיטַעְמָיךְ, לַמׇּחֳרָת מַשָּׂא וּמַתָּן מִי לֵיכָּא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of steps 8–9
steps.terutzResolutionType: Redefining the time frame of the source
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The next day is only for the verdict.
steps.terutzMaskana: The next day can also include discussion, and the ban on switching applies to that discussion.

steps.title: Why doesn't the משנה mention the opposite switch?
steps.stepSummary: The משנה describes judges arguing until a מחייב comes over to the מזכין. If רב is right, the משנה should also describe a מזכה coming over to the חובה side.
steps.simpleTranslation: Come and hear: They debate, these against those, until one of the judges who say 'guilty' sees the point of those who say 'innocent'. If רב is right, let it also teach the opposite!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a new challenge to רב. It uses the continuation of the משנה about judges deadlocked by a majority of only one.
steps.deeperAnalysis: At this stage the judges are deciding the verdict. The משנה mentions only someone switching from חובה to זכות. If רב allows switching from זכות to חובה at the verdict stage, the משנה should have mentioned that case too.

phrases.english: Come and hear:
They debate, these against those,
until one of those voting 'guilty' sees
the words of those voting 'innocent'.
And if it is so,
phrases.notes: If רב is right that someone who argued for זכות may switch to חובה.

phrases.english: let it also teach the opposite!

steps.triggerLanguage: תָּא שְׁמַע: דָּנִין אֵלּוּ כְּנֶגֶד אֵלּוּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: A new challenge to רב after the previous one was answered
steps.kashyaTarget: רב's rule that switching from זכות to חובה is allowed at the גמר דין stage
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The משנה mentions only switching toward זכות, which suggests that switching toward חובה is not possible.

steps.title: The משנה prefers examples of זכות
steps.stepSummary: The תנא chose an example of זכות on purpose. Leaving out the חובה case does not mean it is forbidden.
steps.simpleTranslation: The תנא goes looking for cases of זכות; he does not go looking for cases of חובה.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that the משנה's silence proves nothing.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The תנא likes to describe ways of saving the accused, so he gave the זכות example. The opposite switch may still be allowed, exactly as רב said.

keyTerms.meaning: Acquittal, the side of the defense

phrases.english: The תנא is looking for cases of acquittal,
he is not looking for cases of guilt.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of step 11
steps.terutzResolutionType: Explaining the תנא's choice of example
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Leaving out the opposite case means it is forbidden.
steps.terutzMaskana: The תנא simply prefers examples of זכות, so his silence about חובה proves nothing.

steps.title: The student who argued for acquittal and died
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוסי בר חנינא says a תלמיד who argued for זכות and then died is still counted as voting for זכות. If רב is right, maybe he would have switched.
steps.simpleTranslation: Come and hear, as רבי יוסי בר חנינא says: If one of the students argued for acquittal and died, we view him as if he were alive and standing in his place. But why? Let us say: if he were alive, he would have switched!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings another challenge to רב, using רבי יוסי בר חנינא's rule about a תלמיד who died.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The dead student's זכות vote still counts. Under רב, a living judge could switch to חובה at the verdict stage. So why assume this student would have stayed with זכות?

keyTerms.meaning: Students who sit in front of the court
Who argued for acquittal and then died
We view him as if he were alive

phrases.aramaic: תָּא שְׁמַע, דְּאָמַר רַבִּי יוֹסֵי בַּר חֲנִינָא:
phrases.english: Come and hear, as Rabbi Yosei bar Ḥanina says:
One of the students who argued to acquit and died,
we view him as if
he were alive and standing in his place.
But why? Let us say:
if he were alive,
he would have retracted!
phrases.notes: Some versions have the word in square brackets and some don't.

steps.triggerLanguage: תָּא שְׁמַע, דְּאָמַר רַבִּי יוֹסֵי בַּר חֲנִינָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: A third challenge to רב
steps.kashyaTarget: רב's rule that switching from זכות to חובה is allowed at the גמר דין stage
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If switching to חובה were possible, we could not count a dead student's זכות vote, since he might have switched.

steps.title: In fact, he did not switch
steps.stepSummary: We go by what actually happened: the student never switched.
steps.simpleTranslation: Now, at any rate, he did not retract.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that we do not guess what the student might have done. We count the position he actually held.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Switching is allowed under רב, but that does not mean we assume it would happen. The student died still holding זכות, so his vote stays as זכות.

phrases.english: Now, at any rate,
he did not retract.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of step 13
steps.terutzResolutionType: Going by the actual situation rather than a possibility
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Since he could have switched, we cannot count his זכות vote.
steps.terutzMaskana: He never actually switched, so his זכות vote counts.

steps.title: A report from ארץ ישראל that he disagrees with רב
steps.stepSummary: Scholars in ארץ ישראל sent word that רבי יוסי בר חנינא's statement goes against רב. This undercuts the answer in step 14.
steps.simpleTranslation: But they sent from there: according to the words of רבי יוסי בר חנינא, he is taken out of the view of our teacher!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges the answer in step 14. A report says the two opinions really do conflict.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Step 14 claimed that רבי יוסי בר חנינא and רב can agree. But the scholars in ארץ ישראל said his statement disagrees with רב. That suggests the answer was wrong and the challenge to רב returns.

keyTerms.meaning: They sent from there, meaning from ארץ ישראל
Taken out of the view of: disagrees with

phrases.english: But they sent from there:
According to the words of Rabbi Yosei bar Ḥanina,
he is taken out of the view of our teacher!
phrases.notes: In other words, he disagrees with רב.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the answer given in step 14
steps.kashyaTarget: The claim in step 14 that רבי יוסי בר חנינא and רב agree
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A received report says the two disagree, so the attempt to make them agree must be wrong.

steps.title: The correct report: he does not disagree
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא corrects the report: what was actually said is that he does not disagree with רב.
steps.simpleTranslation: It was said: 'He is not taken out.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא fixes the wording of the report from ארץ ישראל, so רב's rule stands.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The report was quoted wrongly. The accurate wording is 'אין מוצא', meaning he does not disagree. So רבי יוסי בר חנינא and רב agree, and the answer in step 14 holds.
steps.whatToRemember: רב's rule survives these challenges. At the גמר דין stage, someone who argued for זכות may switch to חובה. The sources that seemed to forbid this refer to the discussion stage, or simply describe זכות examples, or describe a case where the person never actually switched. One more challenge comes next, in steps 17–18.

phrases.english: 'He is not taken out' was stated.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of step 15
steps.terutzResolutionType: Correcting the wording of the report
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The report said רבי יוסי בר חנינא disagrees with רב.
steps.terutzMaskana: The accurate report says he does not disagree.

steps.title: The ברייתא of the two court scribes
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא is quoted: two scribes stand before the דיינים and write down the words of those who vote for זכות and those who vote for חובה.
steps.simpleTranslation: Come and hear: Two scribes of the judges stand before them, one on the right and one on the left. They write down the words of those who acquit and the words of those who convict.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא quotes a ברייתא about court scribes. This is a setup: in the next step the גמרא will use it to challenge רב.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא says the scribes record both sides, not only one. The גמרא will ask why the זכות side needs to be written down at all. That question is where the challenge to רב comes from.

keyTerms.meaning: The judges' scribes, court clerks who record what is said

phrases.english: Come and hear:
Two scribes of the judges
stand before them,

phrases.aramaic: אֶחָד מִן הַיָּמִין וְאֶחָד מִן הַשְּׂמֹאל,
phrases.english: one on the right and one on the left,
and they write the words of those who acquit
and the words of those who convict.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: After step 16 restored רבי יוסי בר חנינא as not disagreeing with רב, the גמרא brings a new source that may challenge רב.
steps.kashyaTarget: רב's ruling that a judge who argued for זכות may switch to חובה at the final ruling
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Setup only. The ברייתא's detail that זכות reasons are written down will be used in the next step.

steps.title: Why write down the reasons for acquittal?
steps.stepSummary: Writing down the חובה reasons makes sense, because of a possible new reason the next day. But why write down the זכות reasons, unless it is to stop those judges from switching to חובה? That would go against רב.
steps.simpleTranslation: It makes sense to write down the words of those who convict: tomorrow they may see another reason, and the court will need to hold the case over another night. But the words of those who acquit, what is the reason to write them? Isn't it because if they see another reason to convict, we pay no attention to them?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains why the ברייתא challenges רב. The only good reason to record the זכות votes seems to be to lock those judges in so they cannot switch to חובה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Recording the חובה reasons has a clear use: the court can tell if a judge brings a new reason later. For the זכות reasons, the גמרא suggests the purpose is to hold those judges to their vote. If so, a judge who argued for זכות can never switch to חובה, which goes against רב.

keyTerms.meaning: It makes sense for... (this part is fine, but the next part is a problem)
Holding the case over another night before ruling

phrases.english: It makes sense for the words of those who convict,
since tomorrow they may see another reason
and the court will need to hold the case over another night.
But the words of those who acquit, what is the reason?
Isn't it because if they see
another reason to convict,
we pay no attention to them?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Draws the challenge out of the ברייתא quoted in step 17.
steps.kashyaTarget: רב's ruling that one who argued for זכות may switch to חובה at the final ruling
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The only apparent purpose of recording זכות votes is to stop those judges from switching to חובה. That contradicts רב.

steps.title: The real purpose: one reason from two verses
steps.stepSummary: No. The זכות reasons are written down so that two judges who give the same reason from two different פסוקים are not counted as two votes.
steps.simpleTranslation: No. It is so that two judges should not say one reason from two verses.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא rejects the challenge. It gives a different reason for writing down the זכות votes.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The record lets the court check whether two judges are really giving the same reason from different פסוקים. Such a pair counts as only one vote. This purpose has nothing to do with switching sides, so רב still stands.

phrases.english: No,
it is so that two should not say
one reason from two verses.

steps.triggerLanguage: לֹא, כְּדֵי שֶׁלֹּא יֹאמְרוּ שְׁנַיִם טַעַם אֶחָד מִשְּׁנֵי מִקְרָאוֹת
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of step 18.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Gives a different purpose for the detail in the ברייתא
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Recording זכות votes is meant to prevent judges from switching to חובה.
steps.terutzMaskana: Recording is meant to catch two judges giving one reason from two פסוקים, so they are counted as one vote.

steps.title: רבי יוחנן: count them as one
steps.stepSummary: Support for the answer: רבי אסי asked רבי יוחנן about two judges giving one reason from two פסוקים, and רבי יוחנן said they count as only one.
steps.simpleTranslation: As רבי אסי asked רבי יוחנן: If two judges said one reason from two verses, what is the law? He said to him: We count them only as one.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא shows that the rule used in the answer is a real rule, taught by רבי יוחנן.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The answer in step 19 depends on two such judges being counted as only one vote. רבי יוחנן says exactly that. Now the answer stands on a known ruling.

phrases.aramaic: כְּדִבְעָא מִינֵּיהּ רַבִּי אַסִּי מֵרַבִּי יוֹחָנָן:
phrases.english: As Rabbi Asi asked Rabbi Yochanan:
If two said one reason
from two verses, what is the law?
He said to him:
We count them only as one.

steps.triggerLanguage: כְּדִבְעָא מִינֵּיהּ רַבִּי אַסִּי מֵרַבִּי יוֹחָנָן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Backs up the answer of step 19 with רבי יוחנן's ruling.
steps.raayaObject: The rule that two judges with one reason from two פסוקים are counted as one
steps.raayaSupportSource: רבי אסי's question to רבי יוחנן and his answer
steps.whyThisMatters: This sets a basic rule for counting votes in בית דין: the same reason counts once, even if it is drawn from different פסוקים.

steps.title: What is the source for רבי יוחנן's rule?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks where we learn that one reason from two פסוקים counts as only one.
steps.simpleTranslation: From where are these words derived?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks for the source of רבי יוחנן's rule. This sets up the answers that follow.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Now that the rule is established, the גמרא wants to know what it is built on. Two sources will be offered.

keyTerms.meaning: From where are these words (derived)? A request for a source

phrases.english: From where are these words derived?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks for the source of the rule cited in step 20.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The source in the פסוקים for counting one reason from two פסוקים as one

steps.title: אביי: one verse, many reasons, but not the reverse
steps.stepSummary: אביי learns from the פסוק 'God spoke once, twice I have heard' that one פסוק can give many reasons. But one reason does not come from several פסוקים.
steps.simpleTranslation: אביי said: The verse says, 'God spoke once, twice I have heard this, that strength belongs to God.' One verse can produce several reasons, but one reason does not come out of several verses.
steps.whatsHappening: אביי answers the question with a פסוק from תהלים.
steps.deeperAnalysis: God speaks one time, and many meanings are heard from it, so one פסוק can teach several things. The reverse is not true: the same idea is not taught by two separate פסוקים. So if two judges draw one reason from two פסוקים, at least one of them is using a פסוק that does not teach it, and only one vote counts.

phrases.english: Abaye said:
For the verse says:
"God spoke once,
twice I have heard this,
that strength belongs to God."
One verse goes out to several reasons,

phrases.aramaic: וְאֵין טַעַם אֶחָד יוֹצֵא מִכַּמָּה מִקְרָאוֹת.
phrases.english: but one reason does not come out of several verses.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 21.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The פסוק 'אחת דבר אלהים שתים זו שמעתי' teaches that one פסוק yields many reasons, but one reason does not come from several פסוקים.

steps.title: דבי רבי ישמעאל: like a hammer shattering a rock
steps.stepSummary: דבי רבי ישמעאל teach from 'like a hammer that shatters a rock' that one פסוק breaks into many reasons, the way a rock breaks into many pieces.
steps.simpleTranslation: The school of רבי ישמעאל taught: 'And like a hammer that shatters a rock.' Just as this hammer splits into several fragments, so too one verse goes out to several reasons.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a second teaching, from דבי רבי ישמעאל, with a picture from ירמיהו: the word of God is like a hammer smashing a rock into many pieces.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This teaching backs up the first half of אביי's idea: one פסוק gives many meanings. The picture is of one strike that sends out many pieces, just as one פסוק can teach many things.

keyTerms.meaning: The school (study house) of רבי ישמעאל

steps.whatToRemember: The scribes write down the זכות reasons so the court can catch two judges giving one reason from two פסוקים. Such a pair counts as one vote, because one פסוק can teach many things, but one idea does not come from several פסוקים. This answer keeps רב's view safe.

phrases.english: The school of Rabbi Yishmael taught:
"And like a hammer that shatters a rock":
just as this hammer
splits into several fragments,
so too one verse
goes out to several reasons.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Brings a second source, alongside אביי's, for the idea that one פסוק yields many reasons.
steps.raayaObject: The idea that one פסוק yields many reasons
steps.raayaSupportSource: ירמיהו 23:29, 'וכפטיש יפוצץ סלע', as taught by דבי רבי ישמעאל

steps.title: What is an example of one reason from two sources?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks for a concrete case of one reason coming from two different פסוקים.
steps.simpleTranslation: What is a case of one reason that comes from two פסוקים?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא wants a real example of what it means for two judges to give 'one reason from two פסוקים', the case רבי יוחנן counts as one vote. It is setting up רב זביד's answer.
steps.deeperAnalysis: אביי taught that one פסוק can give many reasons, but one reason does not truly come from two פסוקים. Now the גמרא asks what it would look like if someone did bring one reason from two places. That is exactly the case where two judges count as one vote.

keyTerms.meaning: What is the case? What does it look like?

phrases.english: What is the case of one reason
from two verses?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: After the derivation that one reason does not come from several פסוקים, the גמרא asks for a real example of such a case.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: A concrete example of one reason drawn from two different פסוקים.

steps.title: רב זביד points to a משנה about the מזבח
steps.stepSummary: רב זביד answers by quoting a משנה: the מזבח makes holy whatever is fit for it.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב זביד said: like we learned in a משנה: the מזבח makes holy what is fit for it.
steps.whatsHappening: רב זביד begins his answer by quoting a משנה about things that went up on the מזבח. The next two steps bring the two opinions inside that משנה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה says the מזבח 'makes holy' only what is fit for it. So once such a thing goes up, it stays up. The question is what counts as 'fit for it', and that is where רבי יהושע and רבן גמליאל argue.

keyTerms.meaning: As we learned in a משנה
The מזבח makes holy, so the item stays on it

phrases.english: Rav Zevid said: as we learned in a mishna:
The altar makes holy what is fit for it.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Begins the answer to the question of step 24.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The example is found in the משנה about what the מזבח makes holy.

steps.title: רבי יהושע: whatever is fit for the fire stays up
steps.stepSummary: רבי יהושע says anything fit to be burned on the fire, once it went up, does not come down. He learns this from 'העולה על מוקדה'.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יהושע says: anything fit for the fires, if it went up, it does not come down. As it says: 'the עולה on its fire'. Just like an עולה, which is fit for the fires, does not come down once it went up, so too anything fit for the fires does not come down once it went up.
steps.whatsHappening: This is the first opinion in the משנה. רבי יהושע compares everything fit to be burned to the עולה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The word he focuses on is 'מוקדה', the fire. Because the עולה is described as being on the fire, he sets the rule by fire: anything that is normally burned there stays once it went up.

keyTerms.meaning: If it went up, it does not come down
A קרבן that is fully burned

phrases.english: Rabbi Yehoshua says:
Anything that is fit for the fires,
if it went up, it does not come down,
as it says: 'the burnt-offering on its fire'.
Just like a burnt-offering, which is fit for the fires,
if it went up, it does not come down,
so too anything that is fit for the fires,
if it went up, it does not come down.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Brings the first opinion inside the משנה quoted by רב זביד.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Anything fit to be burned on the fire stays on the מזבח once it went up. This is learned from the word 'מוקדה'.

steps.title: רבן גמליאל: whatever is fit for the מזבח stays up
steps.stepSummary: רבן גמליאל says anything fit for the מזבח, once it went up, does not come down. He learns this from 'על המזבח'.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבן גמליאל says: anything fit for the מזבח, if it went up, it does not come down. As it says: 'it is the עולה on its fire on the מזבח'. Just like an עולה, which is fit for the מזבח, does not come down once it went up, so too anything fit for the מזבח does not come down once it went up.
steps.whatsHappening: This is the second opinion in the משנה. רבן גמליאל also compares to the עולה, but he sets the rule by the מזבח instead of the fire.
steps.deeperAnalysis: He reads the next words of the פסוק, 'על המזבח'. So for him the test is whether the item belongs on the מזבח, not whether it is burned. This gives a wider group of things.

keyTerms.meaning: For the מזבח, belonging on the מזבח

phrases.english: Rabban Gamliel says:
Anything that is fit for the altar,
if it went up, it does not come down,

phrases.aramaic: שֶׁנֶּאֱמַר: ״הִיא הָעֹלָה עַל מוֹקְדָה עַל הַמִּזְבֵּחַ״.
phrases.english: as it says: 'it is the burnt-offering on its fire on the altar'.
phrases.notes: Same פסוק as before, ויקרא 6:2, but he reads it all the way to the words 'on the altar'.

phrases.aramaic: מָה עוֹלָה שֶׁהִיא רְאוּיָה לְגַבֵּי מִזְבֵּחַ –
phrases.english: Just like a burnt-offering, which is fit for the altar,
if it went up, it does not come down,
so too anything that is fit for the altar,
if it went up, it does not come down.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Brings the second opinion in the same משנה, which uses a different part of the פסוק.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Anything fit for the מזבח stays on it once it went up. This is learned from the words 'על המזבח'.

steps.title: What do both of them come to include?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks what both רבי יהושע and רבן גמליאל are adding with their learning.
steps.simpleTranslation: And what are both of them including?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks what point the two opinions share. It is setting up the final answer that ties back to 'one reason from two פסוקים'.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Up to now we saw the two opinions as different. This question looks for what they agree on, so we can see the same reason coming from two places.

keyTerms.meaning: They are including, adding to the rule

phrases.english: And what do both of them include?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Looks for the shared result of the two opinions just quoted.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: What both תנאים add with their learning from the פסוק.

steps.title: רב זביד's example: same result, two sources
steps.stepSummary: Both include פסולין, disqualified offerings. One learns it from 'מוקדה' and the other from 'מזבח'. This is the example of one reason from two sources.
steps.simpleTranslation: Disqualified offerings. One master brings it from 'its fire', and the other master brings it from 'the altar'.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that both opinions come to include פסולין, offerings that became disqualified. Each one gets this from a different word, and this finishes רב זביד's example.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The result is the same: a פסול offering that went up does not come down. Only the source is different, 'מוקדה' for רבי יהושע and 'מזבח' for רבן גמליאל. That is 'one reason from two פסוקים'. If two judges argued like this, they would count as just one vote.
steps.whatToRemember: This is רב זביד's proposed example: both רבי יהושע and רבן גמליאל include פסולין, one from 'מוקדה' and the other from 'מזבח'. The next step challenges it, because the two really disagree about blood and libations.
steps.confusionAlert: Both sources are words in the same פסוק, ויקרא 6:2. Here 'two פסוקים' means two different words or parts used as the source. It does not have to mean two separate verses.
steps.whyThisMatters: This is רב זביד's attempt to show what 'one reason from two פסוקים' looks like. The next step tests whether the two sources really teach the identical rule.

phrases.english: Disqualified offerings.
One master brings it from 'its fire',
and the other master brings it from 'the altar'.

steps.triggerLanguage: מָר מַיְיתֵי לַהּ מִמּוֹקְדָה וּמָר מַיְיתֵי לַהּ מִמִּזְבֵּחַ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers step 28 and finishes the example asked for in step 24.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: רב זביד proposes that both תנאים include פסולין from different words, 'מוקדה' and 'מזבח', as an example of one reason from two sources. Step 30 rejects this.

steps.title: But רבי יהושע and רבן גמליאל really disagree
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges רב זביד's example. The end of that same משנה shows that רבי יהושע and רבן גמליאל disagree about blood and libations, so their sources do not teach one identical rule.
steps.simpleTranslation: But there they do disagree! The end of the משנה says: the only difference between רבן גמליאל and רבי יהושע is blood and libations. רבן גמליאל says they do not come down, and רבי יהושע says they come down.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא attacks the example from Step 29. The same משנה says openly that the two תנאים disagree in one case.
steps.deeperAnalysis: An example of 'one reason from two sources' needs two sources that teach exactly the same thing. Here, 'מוקדה' (burned on the fire) and 'מזבח' (fit for the altar) give different results for blood and libations. Blood and libations are put on the מזבח but are not burned. So the two sources are not teaching one identical rule.

keyTerms.meaning: The later part (end clause) of a משנה
The blood and the wine libations
They shall not come down / they shall come down (from the מזבח)

steps.confusionAlert: Both תנאים agree that most פסולין stay on the מזבח. They only split on blood and libations. That one split is enough to show that their two sources do not teach the same rule.

phrases.english: But there they really do disagree,
phrases.notes: 'There' means the משנה רב זביד quoted, with רבי יהושע and רבן גמליאל.

phrases.english: as the latter clause teaches:
There is no difference between the words of Rabban Gamliel
and the words of Rabbi Yehoshua
except for the blood and the libations,
for Rabban Gamliel says: They shall not come down,
and Rabbi Yehoshua says: They shall come down.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks the conclusion of Step 29 that רב זביד's case is an example of one reason from two sources.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The two sources give different results for blood and libations. So they are two different reasons, not one reason taught from two sources.

steps.title: רב פפא brings a different example from a ברייתא
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא drops רב זביד's example. רב פפא starts a new example from a ברייתא of רבי יוסי הגלילי, which begins by quoting a פסוק.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, רב פפא said: like it is taught in a ברייתא. רבי יוסי הגלילי says: From the fact that it says...
steps.whatsHappening: Since רב זביד's example failed, רב פפא offers a new one. This line sets up the next move: the ברייתא and its פסוק continue on the next amud.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The word 'אלא' (rather) shows that the earlier example has been set aside. רב פפא is still answering the same question: where do we find one rule learned from two different פסוקים? Here he only introduces the source; the details come next.

keyTerms.meaning: Rather (we drop the earlier answer and try a new one)
As it is taught (in a ברייתא)
From the fact that it is said (a פסוק is about to be quoted)

phrases.english: Rather, Rav Pappa said:
As it is taught in a baraita:
Rabbi Yosei HaGelili says:
From the fact that it is stated:
phrases.notes: The פסוק he quotes comes right after this, on the next amud.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Replaces רב זביד's example, which Step 30 knocked down, with a new example.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: An example of one rule learned from two different פסוקים.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: רב פפא points to a ברייתא of רבי יוסי הגלילי (the full content continues on the next amud).
